# Inflation

## Measuring inflation

Inflation is a sustained rise in the general level of prices in an economy. It is usually measured by the percentage change in a consumer price index over a year. A consumer price index tracks the cost of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by typical households. Deflation is a sustained fall in the general level of prices.

## Causes and effects

Demand-pull inflation occurs when total demand grows faster than the economy can produce. Cost-push inflation occurs when higher production costs, such as wages or raw materials, are passed on to buyers. Inflation erodes the purchasing power of money, so each unit of currency buys fewer goods. Central banks often respond to high inflation by raising interest rates.
